motivation: Repeated adaptive method development has turned the existing 20-task OOF set into a development benchmark. A fresh task pool is required before another confirmatory claim, and clean solvability must be established before spending attack episodes on a task.

stage1.scope: all AgentDojo v1.2.2 user tasks in banking, slack, travel, and workspace not present in the existing 20-task v2 set
stage1.selection_after_stage1: Within each domain, retain every seed-101 clean success as a confirmation candidate. If more than eight succeed, use a fixed SHA-256 order and keep eight; do not inspect attack outcomes.

stage2.scope: all 77 fresh tasks, expanded before reading seeds 103 or 107 because seed 101 left Travel with only one candidate
stage2.adaptive_change: The original economical plan would have repeated only seed-101 successes. That would condition inclusion on one stochastic run and make Travel unusable. The expanded clean-only census removes that selection bias; no attack outcome has been generated or read.
stage2.retention_rule: At least two clean successes across seeds 101, 103, and 107
stage2.target: identify every clean-solvable fresh task before freezing fresh development and final-test partitions

stage2_result.decision: Do not generate a nominally four-domain fresh attack set under the current function-tags victim protocol; first test a clean-only native-tool protocol repair.

estimated_stage1_cost: 77 episodes; about 46 aggregate GPU-minutes at the measured prior mean of 35.6 seconds per Llama-3.1-70B AgentDojo episode, plus four model loads
